statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58044 is a request desynchronization risk in the Node.js HTTP server: header fields past the server's maxHeadersCount limit were left out of req.headers, req.rawHeaders and req.headersDistinct but still used to frame the message, so a Content-Length header could be hidden from the application while the request body was still read. A Node.js forwarding proxy that rebuilds outbound headers from the visible ones and pipes the body to a reused backend connection can then be desynchronized. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.23.2, released 2026-07-29: the July 2026 security release, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases, lists 22.x among the affected release lines, and the 22.23.2 release notes, https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.2, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/c8525ac3a6 ('http: reject requests exceeding max header count'), which carries CVE-ID: CVE-2026-58044 and is in the v22.23.2 tag and not in v22.23.1. Outside tests it changes only src/node_http_parser.cc, where the request parser now counts header fields against the parser's maxHeaderPairs limit and rejects the request with a header overflow error, answered with HTTP 431, once the limit is passed. The CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58044, names 22.23.1 as the affected 22.x release. The DHI nodejs-22 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from the upstream Node.js release tarball for their version. Each published nodejs-22 package holds one file, /usr/bin/node, a dynamically linked musl program that carries the Node.js JavaScript library and the C++ runtime where this code lives; the nodejs-22-dev subpackages hold C and C++ header files and two .gypi build configuration files under /usr/include/node, and the nodejs-22-doc subpackages hold the node man page and two debugger helper files, gdbinit and lldb_commands.py, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O file in either. We checked the node binary, /usr/bin/node, in every nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 published by 2026-11-27, on x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 22.23.2-r0, 22.23.3-r0, 22.23.4-r0, 22.23.4-r1, 22.23.4-r2 and 22.23.5-r0 report v22.23.2 through v22.23.5 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 22.22.0-r0, 22.22.1-r0, 22.22.2-r0, 22.22.2-r1, 22.22.3-r0, 22.23.0-r0 and 22.23.1-r0 report v22.22.0 through v22.23.1 and are affected. As a check, the maxHeaderPairs property name that the fix's new C++ check reads appears as a separate C string in the node binary of 22.23.2-r0 and every later build on both architectures, and not in any earlier build. We also ran each of these node binaries three times on each architecture (x86_64 under emulation) with an HTTP server whose maxHeadersCount is 4, sending a POST request whose fifth header is Content-Length: 5 followed by a 5-byte body. 22.23.2-r0 and every later build answer 431 Request Header Fields Too Large without calling the request handler; every earlier build passes the request to the handler with Content-Length missing from req.headers and still delivers the 5-byte body. 22.23.2-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
